summary:
We developed VESTA, an offline-first astronaut health monitoring and clinical triage system for deep-space missions. VESTA tracks each crew member against their own pre-flight baseline across cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, cabin atmosphere/radiation, and sleep/cognitive domains.

To address the challenge, VESTA pairs an anatomical body map and 14-day/live telemetry views with an explainable edge correlation engine grounded in NASA’s Risks of Human Spaceflight. It cross-checks multi-domain signals to distinguish conditions such as hypercapnia fatigue, Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), solar particle events, and isolation drift—translating raw biometrics into a Readiness score, operational Go/No-Go clearances (EVA, Robotics, Docking), hoverable NASA HRP clinical rationales, and actionable countermeasures. An interactive onboarding guide and scenario simulator let crews explore and test responses immediately.

VESTA empowers astronauts to detect subtle risks early, understand root causes, and act autonomously.
details: VESTA is an offline-first astronaut health monitoring app built with React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, and IndexedDB for deep-space missions where Earth communication is delayed. It tracks each crew member against their own pre-flight baseline across heart, cabin air/radiation, sleep/cognitive, and bone health, using a local triage engine grounded in NASA’s Risks of Human Spaceflight to spot issues like CO₂ fatigue, SANS fluid shift, radiation spikes, and isolation drift. By turning telemetry into clear Readiness scores, EVA/Robotics/Docking clearances, hoverable risk explanations, and interactive countermeasures, VESTA helps astronauts detect health risks early and act autonomously.
